title: Audit logging schema workshop notes (schema v1 + SIEM export)
content:
Doc purpose
- Capture notes from cross-functional workshop(s) on audit log schema v1 and sensitive-actions taxonomy.
- Emphasis: unresolved questions, naming debates, SIEM requirements, and follow-ups/owners.

Workshops covered in these notes
- 2026-01-09 (primary): Schema v1 shape + field semantics
- 2026-01-23 (follow-up): SIEM export expectations + delivery semantics + private parity

Attendees (rolling)
- Product/Sec&Compliance: Naomi Feldman
- Security Eng: Marcus Lin, Kevin Osei, Hanae Suzuki
- GRC: Olga Petrov
- Platform/Control Plane: Ethan Park
- Observability/Standards: Allison Grant
- Telemetry/Metering: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman
- SRE/Reliability: Sean Gallagher
- Private Deployments: Vivek Kulkarni
- Console/Tooling: Dylan Brooks, Chloe Martin
- API Gateway: Amara Diallo
- Cross-deploy parity: Diego Santos
- Privacy/Legal: Michael Grant

High-level outcomes (what we agreed on)
1) Canonical audit event schema will be versioned (schema_version at top-level) and validated.
2) Flattened top-level fields for SIEM compatibility, with a controlled “extensions” escape hatch (namespaced keys) but avoid deep nesting.
3) Event taxonomy is an explicit registry (event_type enum) with required fields per type (CI lint).
4) Consistent actor/target semantics across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
5) Redaction/data classification is part of schema design, not an afterthought.

Open questions (still unresolved / needs ADR decision)
A) Flattened vs nested object fields
- Debate: some teams prefer nested actor/target objects for readability; SIEM exporters prefer flat fields.
- Concern: nested objects get mangled differently in Splunk/Sentinel/Datadog pipelines; also harder to enforce cardinality budgets.
- Current leaning: keep stable top-level “core” fields flat; allow “ext.*” keys with strict prefixes and allow-lists.
- Action: Allison to propose final guidance aligned with observability standards; Kevin to sanity-check with Splunk/Sentinel assumptions.

B) event_id format + dedupe semantics
- Question: do we mandate ULID vs UUID v4?
- SIEM reality: duplicates will happen if we do at-least-once delivery; customers want a dedupe key.
- Proposed: event_id is globally unique and stable for an action; recommend ULID for sortability (but accept UUID in v1 as long as unique).
- Open: define “idempotency_key” separate from event_id or reuse event_id?
- SRE note: For retries, producers must NOT re-generate event_id per attempt; generate once per audited action.

C) Timestamp fields
- Need: event_time (when action occurred) vs ingested_time (when pipeline received) vs exported_time (when sent to SIEM).
- Agreement: required “event_time” in RFC3339/ISO8601 UTC; optional “ingested_time” set by ingestion service; exporter may add “exported_time” as an extension.
- Open: should “event_time” be called “timestamp” for SIEM convention? (Splunk expects “time” or uses _time mapping.)
- Proposal: Keep event_time; exporters map accordingly.

D) Actor model (user vs service vs system) + impersonation
- Requirements:
  - Must distinguish: human user, API key, service account, internal system.
  - Must capture if action was performed via impersonation / “act-as” / support access.
- Debate: single set of actor_* fields vs two-layer actor/initiator.
- Draft semantics:
  - actor_* = the authenticated principal that made the request (API key, user, service).
  - initiator_* = the human behind a delegated credential (e.g., SSO user who created an API key used later) (optional; careful re: availability).
  - impersonator_* = the entity that assumed another identity (if any).
- Open: best naming: “actor”, “subject”, “principal”, “user”. Security prefers “actor”; GRC ok with actor.

E) Target/resource semantics + diffs
- We need consistent fields for “what changed” and “what it was done to”.
- Debate: capturing full before/after vs diff summary. Risks:
  - PII/secrets leakage in before/after.
  - Cardinality blow-ups and payload size.
- Agreement direction:
  - Required resource_type + resource_id.
  - Optional resource_name (capped, allow-list, or omit by default).
  - Changes captured as a short, structured summary string (e.g., “role permissions updated: added=model.write removed=export.write”), NOT raw config dumps.
- Open: whether we standardize “change_summary” vs “diff” vs “change_set”.

F) Source attribution fields
- Must-have for investigations: source_ip, user_agent, region/POP, request_id/trace_id.
- API Gateway note: source_ip might be a list (x-forwarded-for) but we should store canonical client IP.
- Privacy note: IP address is personal data in many jurisdictions; need justification + retention guidance.
- Current stance: include source_ip (required when available); do not store full XFF chain; keep raw user_agent optional and maybe hashed/normalized.

G) Tenancy and scope fields
- We need consistent tenant_id across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Project-level actions: project_id / workspace_id naming is inconsistent today.
- Agreement: schema should include:
  - tenant_id (required)
  - organization_id (optional; depends on product model)
  - project_id (optional but strongly recommended)
- Open: name choice: org_id vs account_id vs tenant_id. Platform wants tenant_id as canonical.

H) Policy/routing changes (high cardinality risk)
- Policy engine diffs can be large and high-cardinality.
- Agreement: store policy_id and a bounded “policy_change_summary”; do not log full policy JSON.
- Open: should we include a stable hash of the policy document to correlate changes without storing contents?

I) Private deployment: operator identity availability
- Installer/upgrade tooling sometimes runs without a logged-in “user”.
- Options:
  - capture OS user (risky/noisy)
  - require an operator identifier passed at runtime (recommended)
  - use “system” actor with “operator_hint” optional
- Agreement direction: for Private installer events, require operator_type + operator_id when provided; otherwise actor_type=system and include execution_context fields (node_id/cluster_id) as extensions.

SIEM/customer requirements gathered (Kevin + Solutions Engineering feedback)
- Splunk:
  - Top-level keys preferred; nested objects become dotted fields inconsistently.
  - Customers often want “action” or “event_type” + “result” + “user” + “src_ip” + “tenant”.
  - They will map timestamp; do not rename to _time inside the product; exporter can map.
- Azure Sentinel / Log Analytics:
  - JSON ingestion ok; nested sometimes fine but queries get awkward.
  - Strong desire for stable schema_version + event_type; also wants a consistent “operationName”-like field.
- Datadog:
  - Emphasis on tags/dimensions; cardinality constraints are important.
  - Prefer short enumerations over free-form strings.

Cardinality & payload size constraints (Logan/Nadia)
- Avoid free-form strings:
  - event_type must be enum.
  - actor_type enum.
  - result enum (success|failure|unknown).
- Any *name* field (role_name, project_name) should be optional and bounded, or omitted in v1.
- Cap lengths:
  - user_agent max length (e.g., 256) and consider normalization.
  - change_summary max length (e.g., 1024).
- Avoid logging request payloads, prompts, model outputs, or secret material.

Redaction / data classification notes (Michael Grant + Hanae)
- Explicitly do NOT log:
  - API keys, bearer tokens, session cookies, private keys, client secrets.
  - full email addresses unless absolutely required (prefer user_id; optionally include email_hash).
- Email/username:
  - Security wants some human-readable identifier for investigations.
  - Privacy prefers stable internal IDs; if email included, ensure retention limits and access controls.
- Proposed compromise:
  - actor_id required.
  - actor_display_name optional.
  - actor_email optional OR actor_email_hash (sha256 + salt managed by Redwood) for correlating across logs without exposing PII.
- Action: decide if we allow actor_email in schema v1 or keep as extension only.

Delivery semantics / failure handling (SRE + Security)
- We cannot block admin workflows on audit sink outages for all actions (availability).
- But for certain actions (RBAC/credential changes), we may want stronger guarantees.
- Proposed categories:
  - “guaranteed” (buffer locally + retry; fail closed if cannot enqueue?)
  - “best_effort” (do not block; emit async)
- Open: Whether we actually implement fail-closed anywhere in v1 (likely no; too risky) vs implement buffering and alerting and document semantics.
- Strong requirement: include “delivery_mode” field or capture in internal metrics only?

Naming debates (captured verbatim-ish)
- event_type vs action
  - Pro event_type: more explicit taxonomy and versionable registry.
  - Pro action: maps to many SIEM conventions.
  - Decision: event_type as canonical; exporter may duplicate into action.
- tenant_id vs account_id
  - Platform: tenant_id is consistent across products.
  - Sales/CS: customers say “account”.
  - Decision: tenant_id (docs can explain “tenant/account”).
- result vs outcome vs status
  - Observability: “result” is common.
  - Decision: result (success|failure|unknown) + optional error_code/error_message (bounded).

Draft field list we kept coming back to (not final; used for discussion)
Required candidates:
- schema_version
- event_id
- event_time
- event_type
- tenant_id
- actor_type
- actor_id
- source_ip (when available)
- result
Optional candidates:
- request_id, trace_id, admin_action_id
- actor_display_name, actor_email_hash
- impersonator_id, impersonator_type
- resource_type, resource_id
- change_summary
- user_agent (normalized)
- region / deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private)

Sensitive actions taxonomy notes (PM-938 alignment)
- Must cover at minimum:
  - RBAC changes (role create/update/delete, assignment changes)
  - Credential lifecycle (API keys, tokens, SSO config)
  - Export configuration (SIEM destinations, auth changes)
  - Retention/residency settings changes
  - Routing/policy engine changes (fallback, allow-list)
  - Private install/upgrade/rollback/config apply + credential rotation
- Open: do we audit read-only access to audit logs themselves? (Yes, at least export config + access to audit export secrets; “view audit logs” is sensitive in some orgs.)

Decisions to log in ADR (needs write-up)
- Flattened core fields; extensions namespaced.
- event_type registry with lints.
- Correlation IDs standardized: request_id + trace_id; admin_action_id for console workflows.
- Minimal changes representation (summary/hash) rather than full before/after.

Action items / follow-ups (owners + target)
1) Draft canonical schema v1 JSON Schema with required/optional fields and type constraints
- Owner: Marcus Lin
- Support: Allison Grant, Ethan Park
- Track: Linear ENG-4821

2) Event taxonomy registry and required fields by event_type; add build-time lint
- Owner: Sahana Iyer + Marcus Lin
- Track: Linear ENG-4822

3) Decide actor_email vs actor_email_hash policy; document classification + retention
- Owner: Michael Grant + Naomi Feldman
- Support: Olga Petrov
- Target: before schema “v1 final” sign-off

4) Define event_id guidance (ULID vs UUID) and dedupe recommendation for customers
- Owner: Kevin Osei
- Support: Sean Gallagher
- Output: short section in export guidance + schema notes

5) Exporter mapping requirements (Splunk HEC + Sentinel) and field mapping table
- Owner: Kevin Osei
- Track: ENG-4827 + ENG-4836

6) Correlation fields standardization across services (request_id/trace_id/admin_action_id)
- Owner: Nadia Rahman
- Support: Caleb Johnson
- Track: ENG-4830

7) Cardinality budget enforcement proposal (allow-lists + max lengths)
- Owner: Logan Wright
- Support: Allison Grant
- Output: updated “cardinality budget” doc + schema constraints

8) Private installer operator identity approach (what can we collect consistently)
- Owner: Vivek Kulkarni + Diego Santos
- Support: Amina Yusuf
- Track: ENG-4826

9) Delivery semantics ADR draft (at-least-once/buffering; how producers behave during sink outage)
- Owner: Sean Gallagher
- Support: Marcus Lin
- Track: ADR + ENG-4829

Parking lot (topics we didn’t get to)
- Whether to include geo/device fingerprinting fields (likely no; privacy risk)
- Whether to include “reason” field for admin actions (e.g., ticket reference) (nice-to-have but could become high-cardinality; maybe allow as “ext.change_ticket_id” with constraints)
- Standardized error_code catalog (platform-wide) vs per-service

Notes to self (Naomi)
- Ensure the eventual Confluence schema doc has a crisp “what we log / what we do not log” section. Customers keep asking if prompts/model outputs appear in audit logs (answer: no).
- Make sure SOC2 evidence mapping calls out that duplicates are possible and how customers can dedupe using event_id.
- Confirm that “view audit logs” access is itself audited (at least for export config changes + download/export actions).

Appendix: quotes/snippets from the room (paraphrased)
- “If we can’t answer ‘who did what, to which tenant, from where, and did it succeed’ we’re going to lose security reviews.” (Security Eng)
- “If schema changes break queries every release, customers will turn off the feed.” (Solutions/Export)
- “Please don’t make us ship nested JSON into three different SIEMs.” (Exporter)
- “Do not log the before/after policy JSON; you will regret it.” (Observability)
